Definition: reduplicated from G71; a bringing up, i.e. mode of living:--manner of life.
BiblicalUsage: Agoge is a manner of life — a bringing up, the way a person lives day by day — and it appears once, in Paul's charge to Timothy: 'But thou hast fully known my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, charity, patience.' Paul is not pointing to a single act but to a whole life Timothy had watched: the teaching and the living, side by side, for years.
TheologicalSignificance: Paul tells Timothy, you have followed my manner of life — and this word is just the life lived, not a doctrine about living.
